title: What am I missing
author: Ferihehehaha
selftext:
Hi,

I am in a process (madness?) of creating consistent assets for my game (unreleased since 2016). I tried to use Stable Diffusion web UI for AMDGPUs with Lora but ended up with unusable weird shit. I used the same prompts which were provided civitai, also using the triggerwords. 

I am now experimenting with mixboard. I created a character (image #1), than used it to generate a house, a castle and a tree (image #2), all stayed consistent. Since then I can't get consistent results for any prompts (image #3), I always set the style to the first, character as a reference. Can anyone guide me where to start, I am overwhelmed by the guides, and I event completed a few, but the result is always something else than what I expect.

comments.author: Old-Wolverine-4134
comments.body: Well, you can't really. You can get close using style reference or something like that.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body: The only way to have a high chance of getting consistent results is to either fine tune a local model or use an existing fine tuned model in the style you want. You can then also combine it with other techniques such as img2img and Ipadapters.

comments.author: morefloordoor
comments.body: My favourite part of this post is that not even the first images are consistent. The helmet has a nose bridge, the foot has an extra toe, and the shot from the back has the cape flowing in the wrong direction.

comments.author: Darknessborn
comments.body: Try pixellab but getting serious art for a commercial game is still just not viable imo, and I've spent the last 18m trying haha

replies.author: Ferihehehaha
replies.body: I have a really small game with like 50 assets. Do you think its still not possible?

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: Really depends what you need, like consistent character with animations will be tough. I've just put my [First game](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4340400/Remember_to_Die/) live which has about 450 assets and it took like a year to get them all right, no animations either and over 400 hours in aseprite tidying them up. For the same price as your sub you could commission something on fiver or just buy assets from itch.

replies.author: Ferihehehaha
replies.body: Nice. Thats not so encouraging. But usefu infk, thanks

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: Honestly there are so many free or super cheap assets that I'd just use those while you build your game and make it super fun, then if you're not good at art like me, either practice or commission some art

replies.author: Ferihehehaha
replies.body: Y, maybe hthats the way, i have very specifix stuff though, so i dont think ill find em as an asset pack.but maybe i get in touch with the creator
